subject: Proposal: short runway top-up vs credit pool for ClearView POC
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@clearview.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: short runway top-up vs credit pool for ClearView POC

Hi Maya,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our conversation, I put together two pragmatic ways to give ClearView a bit more runway to finish the integration tests without committing to a larger reserved contract: a timebox top-up (additional 3 weeks of the same POC configuration) or a credit pool (token/compute credits you can consume over the next 60 days).

Attached: SOW_v1.docx (amendment stub) and pricing_matrix_clearview.xlsx (numbers for both options). High-level: the timebox keeps the existing POC scope and SLAs, we provide a discount on incremental compute days because it's the same environment; the credit pool lets you burst and use different models, but has lower per-unit savings.

Can you confirm which approach purchasing prefers, or if they need a blended option? If useful, we can draft a 1-page amendment for signatures today and get our finance team to split invoicing in two installments.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0187

From: Maya Singh <maya@clearview.com>

Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: short runway top-up vs credit pool for ClearView POC

Sergio —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear options. Procurement copied here; two quick questions before we move to legal:

1) If we take the 3-week timebox top-up, can you guarantee the same concurrency cap we have today (10 concurrent inference sessions) and the same latency SLO? We need the test to match production-like conditions.
2) For the credit pool option, what is the expiration on unused credits? We need at least 60 days.

Also, procurement will need a purchase form and a statement of work that explicitly lists the acceptance criteria for the integration milestone. I have the PO template if you want it.

—Maya
Maya Singh
Head of Data Products | ClearView Analytics
maya@clearview.com

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: short runway top-up vs credit pool for ClearView POC

Sergio — quick internal note on levers:

- Timebox top-up (recommended): 3 weeks, same infra/region, keep concurrency cap at 10. Offer: $18k for 3 weeks (reflects a 22% discount vs public list day rate because it's the same environment). We can add a milestone that if ClearView completes the two integration acceptance tests we waive the last week (effectively 2 weeks paid + 1 week contingent).
- Credit pool: $22k credits, 60-day expiry, lower discount on per-token compute (~12%). Good if they need model-hopping.
- Reserved minimal commit: not ideal here but we can propose a small 3-month 50% capacity commit for a lower monthly rate — ask if they want that in writing.

I've uploaded a short pricing note in Drive (internal). If procurement needs a two-invoice split, lauren can handle. Ben can confirm the concurrency/latency mapping but I think we can commit to the same SLO for the top-up.

—Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@clearview.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposal: short runway top-up vs credit pool for ClearView POC

Maya — thanks. Quick answers inline and formal offer below.

On Mon, Jul 6, 2026 at 11:05 AM Maya Singh <maya@clearview.com> wrote:
> 1) If we take the 3-week timebox top-up, can you guarantee the same concurrency cap we have today (10 concurrent inference sessions) and the same latency SLO?

Yes — ben confirms we can pin the same concurrency cap (10 sessions) and bind the same 95th percentile latency SLO for the additional timebox. We will not alter model weights or quantization profiles during the top-up period.

> 2) For the credit pool option, what is the expiration on unused credits?

Credits expire in 60 days from issue.

Formal offer (pick one):
A) Timebox top-up — 3 weeks POC runway; same infra, concurrency=10, latency SLO matched; price = $18,000. If ClearView completes Integration Test 1 + Test 2 by end of top-up, Redwood refunds the third week (invoice adjusted).
B) Credit pool — $22,000 credits, valid 60 days, no concurrency guarantee, usable across models/regions we already have configured for ClearView.
C) Small reserved bridge — 3-month minimal commit at 35% of a standard small pool; finance needs to prepare numbers if they prefer this.

Attached: updated SOW amendment (SOW_v1.docx) and a DocuSign link to sign option A or B quickly. Let me know procurement preferences on invoice split (50/50 or net30 + net30).

Thanks,
Sergio
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: SOW_v1.docx]

From: procurement@clearview.com
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>, Maya Singh <maya@clearview.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: short runway top-up vs credit pool for ClearView POC

Sergio — procurement here. ClearView approves Option A (3-week timebox top-up) on the following commercial terms:

- Price: $18,000 total.
- Invoice split: 60% due on signature, 40% due on completion of integration acceptance (we will sign the amended SOW once legal approves).
- Contingent free week: we accept the milestone waiver for week 3, but require written acceptance criteria for Test 1 and Test 2 in the SOW.
- SOC2 evidence: please send the SOC2 Type II report and current penetration test summary (or a secure link).

Attached: completed PO_Request_Form.pdf with our internal approver info. Send the updated SOW with acceptance criteria and a DocuSign link.

Thanks,
ClearView Procurement
